maxOriginalBytes.reason: 1/5/10/20 MiB padded-input ladder passed on both hosts; bound encoded input bytes, not all high-entropy photos.

maxDecodedPixels.reason: 48 MP (8000x6000) single and eight serial cases at final 3200/.9 passed on both hosts; final iPhone timeline observed about 963 MB total from about 757 MB baseline, with one active decoder/canvas. This is an engineering admission ceiling for the measured path, not a universal safety threshold.

maxImagesPerTurn.reason: Eight serial 48 MP inputs pass at the final edge/quality; actual per-output and aggregate byte admission still applies.

maxVariantBytes.reason: Final largest observed iOS output 1,769,870 B fits 4 MiB; output budget rejects, rather than silently reducing quality indefinitely.

maxRequestImageBytes.reason: Final eight-image total is 14,158,960 B on iOS and 7,646,288 B on Desktop; both fit 24 MiB. Not every eight-image input is promised to fit.

processingTimeoutMs.reason: Final single/eight durations are 162/789 ms iOS and 511/2335 ms Desktop; 15 s is an enforced conservative timeout. Real callback withholding/late replay tests prove cleanup paths, not universal latency.

cacheMaxBytes.reason: 64 MiB is the smallest of three successful real IDB capacities on both hosts, with persisted key/count/Blob bytes/hash, lease, eviction and reopen verification. No evidence justifies default 128/256 MiB.

maxPreviewEdge.reason: 1536 is the smallest tested preview edge; previews are never used to claim fine-text readability.

maxProviderEdge.reason: 3200 replaces the earlier 2048 candidate after visual small-text comparison and final one/eight 48 MP resource confirmation. Source content above 3200 with tiny text remains a known readability boundary.

jpegQuality.reason: Use .9 as the tested higher-quality starting point; enforce actual encoded Blob bytes because host JPEG outputs differ.

boundaries: No universal device safety guarantee. The final iPhone timeline sampled 962,676,736 B total and retained about 68 MB above its own prior baseline after final GC; host/allocator/GC capacity contributions are not isolated.

One actual critical MemoryPressureEvent is retained. It is 67 seconds after the resource run and 0.320 seconds after visibilitychange while moving Obsidian to background. Official WebKit proactively releases critical memory on suspension; origin remains an inference, not an OS OOM claim or a fabricated no-pressure pass.
The final 3200/.9 one/eight-image confirmation uses a repeated synthetic 48 MP JPEG. Eight distinct high-entropy photos, HDR and large HEIC-specific decoder peaks are not certified by it.

Source images wider than 3200 with tiny text may lose readability. 3200 is the default provider edge, not a promise of arbitrary screenshot transcription. Formal HEIC JPEG export remains a separate rendering policy.
Safari samples inspected WebContent memory, not exact whole-device or allocation peaks. The single 162 ms iOS case had no in-window 0.5 s Memory sample; the eight-image case did.
JavaScript memory classification includes allocated GC block capacity and tracked extra/external memory, not only surviving objects; nonzero post-GC footprint alone does not establish a leak.

Actual browser quota exhaustion was not attempted or observed; injected QuotaExceeded tests are separately labeled. Cache cursor/count/hash prove logical persistence rather than exact OS disk or resident allocation.
Cache cleanup leaves originals and formal attachments untouched; four named source hashes and final 48 MP source hash were verified unchanged.
Production Chat draft preservation, integrated migration, provider behavior and real output-quality policy remain later-phase integration work; P0 demonstrates independent feasibility.

interpretation: UI 828.20 MB is 828,196,864 bytes total; it occurs about 32 seconds after resources finish, so it is not a 48 MP-only peak.
The 48 MP ladder has three unambiguously in-window samples; maximum is 707,954,688 bytes. About 0.5 s sampling can miss shorter native peaks.
Pre-run stable observed footprint is about 374 MB. The combined test does not return to this baseline during the exported recording.

High retained categories are JavaScript and Other. Images has a small nonzero observation during processing and is zero in the later baseline/peak samples; zero in that category cannot be read as no native image allocations.

The runner keeps only scalar reports/output paths globally. No global Blob/ArrayBuffer/base64 list is intentionally retained. Temporary 4 MiB buffers and Blob cache fill allocate heavily. Several page full-GC records appear after resources finish, while the category reports allocated capacity rather than only live objects; this is not by itself proof of a leak.

Screenshot/CPU/Memory/JS instruments were active, and many output files were created. Their memory effects are not isolated by this capture; neither instrumentation nor Obsidian can be assigned causal ownership without stronger evidence.

Cache 64/128/256 are sequential temporary databases. Cursor byte totals are logical persistence evidence, not resident memory. Whole recording later peak is not evidence that 256 MiB default is appropriate.

pressureInterpretation.fact: One critical event occurs outside the resource run, after a blur/visibilitychange during transition from Obsidian to Files. No manual simulated pressure action was performed.
pressureInterpretation.inference: Consistent with proactive background suspension memory release. The event carries severity, not origin, so it does not establish OS low-memory/OOM or prove a unique cause.
pressureInterpretation.sourceVersionBoundary: Current official WebKit source explains the possible path; installed iOS binary call provenance was not captured.

manualActions.action: Collect garbage near end of recording

conclusions: Both hosts complete single and eight serial 48 MP inputs at 3200/.9 within the enforced output and aggregate budgets; original hash is unchanged and owned image/canvas/URL references return to zero.

The second recording has no screenshot records. About 963 MB observed total includes about 757 MB already-open host baseline; observed increase is about 205 MB, not eight simultaneously decoded 48 MP buffers.

After final full GC the median remains about 825 MB, about 68 MB above this recording baseline. GC-owned capacity/native caches/host state are not isolated; this residual is retained as a limitation, not called fully released or a proven leak.

The one critical event is retained explicitly and occurs during background transition, not the resource case. It is consistent with proactive background cleanup and does not itself invalidate 48 MP/8-image processing evidence.
Engineering defaults are closed for the tested static-image path. They are not universal safety guarantees, and production lifecycle/recovery validation remains necessary.
